$note: The stored-document grammar contract holds one row per path and value class, per parameter-list
and workflow-row field, and per rule. Each row carries a `state`:
`clicked`, `prevented`, `opened` and `hostSlot` name a test (`test`) in the playground suite whose title carries
`@row:<id>`; `hostSlot` also names the slot (`slot`) the value is authored through. `deferred` marks a form the editor cannot author yet;
it carries a `why` saying what is not supported yet. `exempt` is only for `structure`, `compilation-fault` and
`definition-undrawable`. `gap` is not covered yet, and the release job refuses a contract holding one.
A row id is its path with each space written as a dash, then the value class: `node.id#absent`. The
paths and their kinds are regenerated from StoredVersionComparison.Fields and from packages/core's
kind table; the value classes the kind table does not derive are named here: a blank
or dotted name, an empty id, a `sources` or `outputPorts` entry the block does not declare, a `type`
that is neither `direct` nor `literal`, `defaultOutputJson` that is not the text of a JSON object,
and a port list written as `""` or `null`.
A configuration's values carry `value-`, because the field itself is an object, nullable and optional.
The objects array holds every object kind for the unlisted key the reader refuses there.
The workflow row holds the fields a create and an update take (Editor/WorkflowEditorContracts.cs:13-47),
including the two stored parameter lists, whose blank and null spellings the reader refuses.
